On the first calculation step after `accept`, the padded rate block has just been XORed into the persistent state and is being evaluated by the two-round Keccak network. Probing `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.c[4][0]` in this early-round window exposes an internal representation before all 24 rounds have diffused the input. The observation leaks lane-level information about the secret input that is not present as a directly accessible architectural signal.

On subsequent `calc` cycles, feedback from the registered permutation output re-enters the same combinational round network. Sampling `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.c[4][0]` at a fixed cycle offset across repeated operations supplies aligned intermediate values for differential or correlation analysis. Combining those observations can recover secret-dependent relationships even when a single lane observation is insufficient to reconstruct the input.
